name: Battery
description: AGM battery located in the trunk on most E70 diesels, with a jump/positive terminal post in the engine bay. Always disconnect first and reconnect last.
removalSteps: Switch off ignition and remove key from vicinity of vehicle.
Disconnect negative terminal first, insulate the clamp.
Disconnect positive terminal, insulate the clamp.
Remove battery hold-down clamp.
Lift battery out, keeping it upright.
inspectionPoints: Battery date code vs vehicle age
commonMistakes: Disconnecting positive before negative (risk of short circuit against body)
Forgetting battery registration/coding after replacing with a new battery
Not noting radio/infotainment codes before disconnect
reconnectChecklist: Terminals clean and corrosion-free
Negative connected last
Hold-down clamp torqued and secure
Battery registered via coding tool if replaced
Confirm all comfort electronics (windows, sunroof) relearned

name: ECU Box (DDE)
description: Digital Diesel Electronics (DDE) control unit housing at the rear of the engine bay near the firewall. Controls fuel injection, turbo boost, glow plugs, and emissions.
removalSteps: Disconnect battery per Battery section first.
Release ECU box cover latches.
Disconnect main harness connectors — label each with wire label system before removal.
Unbolt ECU box mounting bracket.
Lift ECU/box assembly clear.
commonMistakes: Swapping ECU between vehicles without ISN (immobilizer sync) matching
Not labeling multi-pin connectors before disconnect
Forcing connector latches — BMW connectors release with a specific pull/lever motion
reconnectChecklist: All harness connectors fully seated and latched
Box cover sealed
Ground straps to ECU bracket reconnected
Read fault codes after first power-up

name: Intake System
description: Air intake tract from airbox through MAF sensor to turbo inlet, including intake resonator and ducting.
removalSteps: Release intake ducting clamps.
Disconnect MAF sensor electrical connector.
Remove airbox lid and filter.
Unbolt airbox base if full removal needed.
inspectionPoints: Ducting cracks or loose clamps (boost/vacuum leak source)
Oil residue inside intake (may indicate turbo seal wear)
commonMistakes: Leaving intake clamps loose causing unmetered air / boost leaks
Debris left in intake tract during engine-out work
reconnectChecklist: All ducting clamps tight
MAF connector seated
New air filter installed
No foreign objects in intake path before first start

name: MAF Sensor
description: Mass Air Flow sensor measuring intake air volume, mounted in the intake ducting ahead of the turbo inlet.
removalSteps: Disconnect electrical connector — label as its own wire ID.
Loosen retaining clamp or screws.
Slide sensor out of housing carefully — hot-wire element is fragile.
commonMistakes: Touching or cleaning the wire element with the wrong solvent
Forcing sensor housing causing element damage
reconnectChecklist: Sensor fully seated and clamped
Connector latched
Confirm live MAF data via diagnostic tool after first start

name: MAP / Boost Sensor
description: Manifold Absolute Pressure sensor reading intake manifold boost pressure, used by the DDE for turbo boost control.
removalSteps: Disconnect electrical connector — label wire ID.
Remove single retaining screw or clip.
Withdraw sensor from manifold port.
commonMistakes: Reusing a damaged O-ring causing false boost readings
reconnectChecklist: Seated fully in manifold port
Connector latched
Live boost data plausible at idle/rev after first start

name: Glow Plug Controller
description: Relay/control module managing glow plug preheat timing for cold starts, mounted on or near the intake manifold.
removalSteps: Disconnect battery first.
Disconnect main harness connector — label wire ID.
Disconnect individual glow plug leads.
Unbolt controller from mounting bracket.
commonMistakes: Mixing up individual glow plug lead order
Not checking for a related fault code before condemning the controller
reconnectChecklist: All 6 glow plug leads reconnected to correct cylinder
Main connector latched
Glow plug cycle confirmed via diagnostic tool

name: Fuel Injectors
description: Piezo/solenoid common-rail injectors, one per cylinder, mounted through the cylinder head under the valve cover.
removalSteps: Relieve fuel system pressure per manufacturer procedure.
Disconnect injector electrical connectors — label each wire ID by cylinder number.
Remove fuel rail per Fuel Rail section.
Remove injector clamp bolts (see torque spec TQ-016).
Extract injectors with a suitable puller — do not pry.
inspectionPoints: Injector code label legible for ECU coding
commonMistakes: Reusing old injector seal washers (causes combustion leak)
Not recording injector correction codes before install — required for ECU coding
Contaminating injector tips/holes with debris
reconnectChecklist: New seal washers fitted
Clamp bolts torqued per TQ-016 with angle stage
Injector correction codes entered into ECU via diagnostic tool
Leak-off return lines reconnected

name: Fuel Rail (High Pressure)
description: Common rail fuel distribution manifold feeding all 6 injectors at high pressure from the HP fuel pump.
removalSteps: Relieve system pressure and clean area to prevent contamination.
Disconnect rail pressure sensor connector — label wire ID.
Disconnect high pressure supply line from pump.
Disconnect individual injector high pressure lines.
Remove rail mounting bolts (TQ-015) and lift rail clear.
inspectionPoints: High pressure line sealing surfaces for damage
commonMistakes: Any dirt ingress into open fuel lines — cap immediately when disconnected
Reusing crush washers/seals on high pressure line fittings
reconnectChecklist: All high pressure line fittings torqued evenly
Rail mounting bolts torqued per TQ-015
Pressure sensor connector latched
System primed and checked for leaks before full start

name: Turbocharger System (sequential twin-turbo)
description: Small high-pressure and large low-pressure turbochargers operating sequentially, mounted at the front of the engine on the exhaust manifold.
removalSteps: Drain coolant if turbo is water-cooled at this stage.
Disconnect oil feed and return lines — cap immediately.
Disconnect vacuum actuator lines — label each.
Remove exhaust manifold nuts (TQ-011).
Remove turbo-to-downpipe connection.
Support and remove turbo assembly.
inspectionPoints: Shaft play (radial and axial) on both turbos
Oil residue in compressor housing (seal wear indicator)
commonMistakes: Not priming oil feed before first start (causes dry startup bearing wear)
Reusing manifold gaskets/nuts instead of new ones
Mixing up small/large turbo oil and vacuum line routing
reconnectChecklist: Oil feed line primed and torqued per TQ-012
Manifold nuts torqued per TQ-011
Vacuum actuator lines correctly routed and labeled
Boost leak test performed after start

name: Vacuum Lines
description: Vacuum hose network controlling turbo actuators, intake flaps, and EGR components.
removalSteps: Photograph/label routing before disconnecting anything.
Disconnect each line at the manifold and component end, labeling with wire/hose ID.
Cap open ports to prevent debris ingress.
inspectionPoints: Cracking, hardening, or collapse of hose material
commonMistakes: Misrouting lines causing turbo actuator faults or limp mode
Reusing brittle old vacuum hose
reconnectChecklist: All lines matched to labeled IDs
No kinks or pinch points
Vacuum system holds pressure on smoke/vacuum test

name: Coolant Hoses
description: Upper/lower radiator hoses, heater core hoses, and turbo coolant lines forming the cooling circuit.
removalSteps: Drain cooling system fully into a clean catch container.
Release hose clamps at each end.
Label each hose with its wire/hose ID before removal.
inspectionPoints: Clamp condition — replace spring clamps with worm-drive if reused often
commonMistakes: Air pockets left in system after refill (diesel cooling systems need proper bleed procedure)
Reusing degraded factory hose clamps
reconnectChecklist: All hoses matched to correct ports
Clamps secure
System bled per Cooling System chapter procedure
No leaks after warm-up cycle

name: Radiator
description: Primary coolant radiator at the front of the radiator support pack, ahead of the intercooler and condenser.
removalSteps: Drain coolant.
Disconnect upper/lower hoses.
Disconnect fan shroud and electrical connectors if equipped.
Remove radiator mounting bolts (TQ-013).
Lift radiator clear, protecting fins.
inspectionPoints: End tank cracking (plastic tanks are common failure point)
commonMistakes: Overtightening plastic end tank fittings
Bending fins during reinstall
reconnectChecklist: Mounts torqued per TQ-013
Hoses reconnected and clamped
Fan shroud aligned and secure
System refilled and bled

name: Intercooler
description: Charge air cooler mounted in the front bumper support, cooling compressed air between turbo stages and the intake manifold.
removalSteps: Remove front bumper or access panel per chapter procedure.
Disconnect charge pipes at both ends.
Remove mounting brackets.
Lift intercooler clear.
inspectionPoints: Oil residue inside core (turbo seal wear indicator)
commonMistakes: Not clamping charge pipes fully — boost leak after reassembly
Cross-contaminating intercooler core with oil residue not cleaned before reinstall
reconnectChecklist: Charge pipes clamped tight both ends
Mounting brackets secure
Boost leak test performed

name: Cooling Fan Assembly
description: Electric or viscous-clutch fan assembly mounted behind the radiator, drawing air through the radiator pack.
removalSteps: Disconnect fan electrical connector or unbolt viscous clutch (special tool, opposite thread).
Remove fan shroud retaining clips.
Lift fan assembly clear.
commonMistakes: Using wrong rotation direction on viscous clutch removal tool (left-hand thread on many BMW fans)
reconnectChecklist: Fan spins freely without shroud contact
Connector latched
Fan activation confirmed via diagnostic tool or thermal test

name: Engine Mounts
description: Left and right hydraulic engine mounts connecting the block to the front subframe, isolating vibration.
removalSteps: Support engine securely with hoist or under-engine support before removal.
Remove mount-to-bracket bolts (TQ-008).
Remove mount-to-subframe bolts (TQ-007).
Lift mount clear.
commonMistakes: Removing both mounts simultaneously without engine support — engine can shift and damage components
Under-torquing mount bolts after engine settles onto them
reconnectChecklist: Mounts torqued per TQ-007 and TQ-008
Engine sits level, no strain on hoses/lines
Recheck torque after engine settles under its own weight

name: Transmission Bellhousing
description: Interface between engine and ZF 6-speed automatic transmission, housing the torque converter.
removalSteps: Support transmission independently before separating from engine.
Remove torque converter bolts through inspection cover (TQ-010).
Remove bellhousing bolts (TQ-009).
Carefully separate engine and transmission, keeping them aligned on dowels.
commonMistakes: Letting transmission hang unsupported on the input shaft
Torque converter not fully seated before bolting to flexplate — measure gap first
reconnectChecklist: Torque converter confirmed fully seated before bolt-up
Bellhousing bolts torqued per TQ-009
Converter bolts torqued per TQ-010
Transmission fluid level checked after reassembly

name: Grounding Straps
description: Engine-to-body and engine-to-chassis ground straps critical for reliable CAN bus communication, glow plug operation, and starter current path.
removalSteps: Note strap locations and label each with a wire ID.
Remove strap mounting bolts (TQ-026).
Set aside straps for cleaning.
commonMistakes: Skipping straps during reassembly — causes intermittent electrical faults that are hard to diagnose later
Painting over ground points instead of masking them
reconnectChecklist: All mating surfaces cleaned to bare metal
Straps torqued per TQ-026
Continuity checked with multimeter engine-to-body and engine-to-battery negative

name: Engine Wiring Harness
description: Main engine harness routing power, ground, and signal wiring to sensors, injectors, glow plugs, and the DDE.
removalSteps: Work systematically front-to-back, labeling every connector using the Wire Labeling System before disconnecting.
Release harness clips and conduit from brackets.
Free harness from engine and lift clear with connectors protected.
inspectionPoints: Chafed or melted insulation, especially near turbo/exhaust heat sources
commonMistakes: Not labeling connectors before removal — leads to guesswork on reassembly
Routing harness too close to hot turbo components on reinstall
reconnectChecklist: Every connector matched to its labeled ID and marked reinstalled
Harness clipped clear of heat sources and moving parts
Full fault code scan performed after first start to confirm no open circuits
